Prelude.description: Implicitly imported module holding the core types and functions. Hide it with `import Prelude ()`.

Maybe.signature: data Maybe a = Nothing | Just a
Maybe.description: Optional value. Its Monad instance short-circuits on Nothing.

Either.signature: data Either a b = Left a | Right b
Either.description: A value of one of two types; by convention Left is the failure.

IO.description: A description of an effectful computation. Composed purely, run only by `main`.

Functor.signature: class Functor f where fmap :: (a -> b) -> f a -> f b

Monad.signature: class Applicative m => Monad m where (>>=) :: m a -> (a -> m b) -> m b
Monad.description: Sequencing with dependency on earlier results.

Foldable.description: Reduction over a container: foldr, foldMap, length, sum.

Traversable.signature: class (Functor t, Foldable t) => Traversable t

Semigroup.signature: class Semigroup a where (<>) :: a -> a -> a

Monoid.signature: class Semigroup a => Monoid a where mempty :: a

Text.description: Compact, strict UTF-16 text. Prefer it to String for real work; String is a lazy list of Char.

ByteString.description: Packed bytes. Use it for binary data and network payloads, not for text.

Map.description: Immutable ordered map, a size-balanced tree. O(log n) lookup and insert.

Vector.description: Immutable O(1)-index array with fusion. `Data.Vector.Unboxed` avoids boxing.

IORef.description: Mutable reference in IO. Use `modifyIORef'` to avoid thunk build-up.

MVar.description: A mutable box that is either full or empty, used as a lock or a one-place channel.

STM.description: Composable memory transactions over TVars, run by `atomically`.

Async.description: A handle to a concurrent action, from the async package. `concurrently` and `race` are the usual entry points.

State.description: Threads a state value through a computation purely.

ExceptT.description: Adds typed failure to another monad.

bracket.signature: bracket :: IO a -> (a -> IO b) -> (a -> IO c) -> IO c
bracket.description: Acquire/release with exception safety. `finally` and `bracket_` are the simpler forms.

catch.signature: catch :: Exception e => IO a -> (e -> IO a) -> IO a
catch.description: Handles a synchronous exception. Never catch all exceptions in a worker thread.

evaluate.description: Forces a value to WHNF inside IO, so a pure exception surfaces where you can catch it.

seq.description: Forces the first argument before returning the second.

deepseq.signature: deepseq :: NFData a => a -> b -> b
deepseq.description: Forces a value completely, not just to WHNF. `force` returns it.

GADTs.description: Lets constructors carry their own type refinements, so pattern matching learns type equalities.

OverloadedStrings.description: Makes string literals polymorphic via IsString, so they work as Text or ByteString.

DerivingVia.description: Derives an instance by reusing another type's, through a representationally equal newtype.

TypeFamilies.description: Functions at the type level, associated with a class or standalone.

main.description: Program entry point. The only place the runtime actually performs the described effects.
